Meeting Header:

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh 45 minute block today, we've got a pretty focused agenda around the canary and go-live planning. are we good on time?
[00:12] Laura: yes thanks, quick yes from me. the execs want a clear rollback and a monitoring playbook — important for HIPAA auditors so we need audit logs, KMS usage, that sort of thing.
[00:25] Mike: yep, and cost matters too; we can't exceed our projected token spend during the canary.
[00:33] Samir: great, i'll start with a quick recap of the POC results so far, then we'll jump into the cutover plan.
[00:40] Samir: (SE) last week the throughput tests looked good, p50 at ~80ms, p95 around 220ms on our dedicated pool, p99 was a little spiky when requests hit longer contexts. we saw KV cache hits for ~45% of requests which helped cost, though the K V cash (transcription) word showed up in the logs a few times —
[01:05] Laura: just to clarify, p99 spiky periods aligned with batch size changes right? we had batch tuning at 128 vs 64 which changed tail latency.
[01:13] Samir: exactly, when we lowered batching we reduced tail but throughput dropped, so it's a tradeoff — latency vs cost.
[01:20] Alex: classic. for the go-live we should pin a profile that matches your SLA: 200ms p95 and under 500ms p99, if we can hit that with dedicated and modest batching, we can be comfortable.
[01:33] Priya: SRE question — for the private deployment we need VPC peering and KMS keys in our account, can Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[01:41] Alex: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private; for Dedicated we can provide bring-your-own-KMS patterns. we'll include specific IAM perms in the runbook.
[01:51] Mike: what about telemetry — we'd like traces in our Grafana and alerts for error-rate and latency SLO breaches.
[01:58] Samir: we'll push traces via OpenTelemetry, and we can wire up a Grafana dashboard. i'll share a pre-built dashboard and the alert rules.
[02:06] Laura: good. what's the canary cadence you're proposing? 0->5->25->100% over 48 hours? or a faster ramp?
[02:14] Alex: suggested plan from Redwood: start with internal traffic only for 6 hours, then 5% for 4 hours, 25% for 12 hours, 100% if healthy. total ~24-48h depending on metrics. the key stop gates are: error-rate <0.5% sustained, p95 < 250ms, token cost within threshold, and no security alerts.
[02:34] Mike: can we run an A/B concurrently to compare the new model vs current fallback model? we want quality comparisons.
[02:41] Samir: yes, A/B is supported — we can route 10% to Redwood model and 90% to baseline and compare quality metrics (BLEU-ish, but we'll use custom prompt evals). note: that will double telemetry complexity but doable.
[02:56] Priya: how do you handle fallbacks automatically? if the model spikes in latency do you have auto-failover?
[03:02] Alex: we have automated fallback policies - route to a lighter model or to your pre-prod endpoint. we can configure thresholds for immediate fallback (e.g., p99 > 750ms for 1 minute triggers fallback).
[03:13] Laura: and for compliance the audit log needs to show who triggered rollbacks and exact request ids for sampled traffic.
[03:20] Samir: audit logs are available, though sometimes the transcription in the logs calls the product Redwood Inference 'Redwoood' so ignore that, haha — logs are real though.
[03:31] (laughter)
[03:36] Alex: on runbooks: we'll provide a canary runbook with steps: pre-checks (connectivity, KMS, IAM, smoke test), ramp steps, monitoring checks, rollback steps, and post-cutover verification.
[03:48] Mike: can you include a manual rollback command and automated option? we might require manual for the first cutover.
[03:55] Samir: yes manual + automated. automated will do immediate switch to fallback model; manual will be documented with CLI and console steps.
[04:04] Laura: what logs will be retained? auditors will ask for 90 days.
[04:09] Alex: we have configurable retention. for Private we can set long retention in your S3, for Hosted we offer add-on retention packages. we'll send the compliance pack.
[04:20] Priya: technical deep-dive question — during the canary do you support continuous batching and dynamic kernel selection? earlier we hit an issue where kernels warmed up and caused spikes.
[04:31] Samir: yes, runtime supports continuous batching and kernel selection, but there is a warm-up period. for the canary we'll pre-warm with synthetic traffic to avoid first-hour spikes. we'll include that in the runbook.
[04:42] Alex: regarding cost — we'll estimate token cost for the canary and provide a spreadsheet. remember quantization and KV cache savings will affect unit costs.
[04:51] Mike: please make the cost spreadsheet conservative.
[04:55] Samir: noted. we'll provide both optimistic and conservative estimates.
[05:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible) question on SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[05:05] Alex: yes SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported; seeding RBAC roles for the SRE and ML folks is straightforward — we'll share a sample admin policy.
[05:15] Laura: ok, let's talk about metrics we'll monitor during each ramp stage so we have clear gates.
[05:20] Samir: primary metrics: request success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (4xx/5xx), throughput (rps), token consumption per request, and model quality indicators (regression tests on eval prompts). secondary: resource utilization and batch sizes.
[05:36] Priya: who owns alert tuning? we don't want noisy alerts.
[05:40] Alex: Redwood will propose alerts, but ownership shifts to BrightPath post-cutover. we'll agree on thresholds in the runbook.
[05:47] Mike: for the A/B quality evals, can you run automated prompt sets and provide a report?
[05:52] Samir: yes we have an eval harness — we'll run the golden prompts and produce a regression report; if degradation > X% we won't promote. we'll agree the X threshold in the next call.
[06:04] Laura: timeline question — if the canary starts on Monday (2026-08-16), when would you expect full cutover?
[06:11] Alex: if all gates pass we can do full cutover by Wednesday (2026-08-18). conservative plan is Thursday to allow stakeholder review.
[06:20] Mike: OK. risk: vendors mentioned — what if Anthropic or Vertex becomes cheaper mid-run?
[06:26] Alex: we can set routing policies by cost tier; Redwood can route to cheaper variants if latency/cost profile is acceptable. but for compliance you might want pinned versions.
[06:36] Priya: let's capture the exact cutover steps now — pre-cutover checklist, canary steps, rollback, post-verify.
[06:42] Samir: pre-cutover: VPC peering verified, KMS keys accessible, SSO/RBAC set, smoke tests pass, dashboard deployed. canary: internal 6h -> 5% 4h -> 25% 12h -> 100% if gates pass. rollback: immediate fallback to baseline model or freeze traffic; we have CLI commands and console UI steps. post-verify: run 50 sample eval prompts and check quality metrics + end-to-end tracing.
[07:09] Laura: for the manual rollback we need a runbook excerpt that our on-call can follow exactly — step-by-step.
[07:16] Alex: we'll provide step-by-step and a short one-page playbook for on-call.
[07:21] Mike: please include expected timelines for each step (minutes to revert etc.).
[07:26] Samir: repro steps for common failures will be included.
[07:30] (brief cross talk)
[07:35] Alex: any other blockers?
[07:37] Priya: only outstanding is VPC peering IAM role creation — i'm blocked until we get the exact list of required IAM perms.
[07:44] Alex: we'll send IAM perms today.
[07:46] Laura: and security team will need SOC2 evidence — can you share SOC2 cert and a list of encryption-in-transit details?
[07:55] Alex: yes, security pack will be shared.
[07:57] Mike: last question on metrics retention for canary data — we want raw request logs for 30 days internally.
[08:04] Samir: we can export logs to your S3; we'll document retention in the runbook.
[08:09] Alex: ok let's recap next steps, action items.
[08:12] (auto-generated action item summary)
[08:20] Alex: thanks all, we'll send the runbook + dashboard + IAM perms by Monday EOB. Samir will kick off the pre-warm and run the 24h canary on Tuesday if Priya confirms VPC connectivity.
[08:32] Laura: sounds good, thanks.
[08:35] Mike: thanks everyone.
[08:38] Alex: bye.

End of transcript.
